title: Verdict for an encoded circuit
statement: For any Boolean parameter $\mathsf{exact}$ and bit strings $\mathsf{code}$ and $x$, the verdict on the pairing of $\mathsf{code}$ with $x$ is true if and only if there exist a natural number $n$ and a directed acyclic Boolean circuit $C$ with $n$ input vertices such that $C$ is well formed with fan-in at most two, its encoding is $\mathsf{code}$, $n\le |x|$, and, if $\mathsf{exact}$ is true, then $n=|x|$, while $C$ evaluates to true on the first $n$ bits of $x$ (taking any out-of-range input lookup to be false).
hypotheses_covered: existence of a natural number $n$ and a circuit with $n$ inputs
the circuit is well formed and has fan-in at most two
the circuit evaluates to true on inputs obtained from $x$, with out-of-range lookups false
